title: Call Stripe before Nov 6: crowdfunding approval and our payout model
description:
Rick, before Nov 6. Stripe's prohibited list includes "Payment facilitation and aggregation (including receiving settlement proceeds for goods or services that you did not provide, on behalf of one or multiple third-party sellers)", and it lists "Crowdfunding platforms" as needing approval from Stripe sales (checked: stripe.com/legal/restricted-businesses).

Tell Stripe what we are: a platform where patrons back creatives' projects, charged on our account, paid to creatives through Connect separate charges and transfers. Ask:
1. Are we approved as a crowdfunding platform, or is Connect enough?
2. Can the $2 per active account fee be reduced while we're small?
3. Any limits on how long we can hold a backing before the creative sets up payouts?

Record the answers in docs/features/backing-payouts.md.

One-time and monthly (a Stripe Checkout subscription can create the customer from the email — likely, verify in test mode). Write the pending projectSupport row without a userId. title: Lawyer/accountant: three backing questions before Nov 6
description:
Rick, before Nov 6. The three questions from docs/features/backing-payouts.md:
1. Is a backing a payment for goods or services? If not, neither the federal payment-processor exemption nor state agent-of-payee rules clearly apply. Does Connect (Stripe holds the money transmitter licenses) fully cover us?
2. Will Stripe classifying us as crowdfunding change anything?
3. Under Connect we file the tax forms. Is it a 1099-NEC or a 1099-K, and is a backing income or a gift to the creative?

Also: state unclaimed-property rules for small balances held under the $50 minimum.

description:
Part 2 of bead wonderwall-7avu step 2. Rick is fine with sending transfers by hand for Nov 6.

It calls stripe.transfers.create to the creative's connected account for what they're owed (sum of backingPayments.workCents minus what's already been paid), with source_transaction set so it waits for funds. It then records a creativePayouts row with the Stripe transfer id. Disabled until the creative's connected account can receive transfers.

The $50 minimum applies to the payout to their bank (the Stripe account setting), not to the transfer.

title: Backing checkout: add card processing on top, paid by the backer
description: Decided 2026-09-18: the platform's 10% (5% above $1,000) comes out of the backing; the payer covers card processing on top (the plan §3). Backing checkout adds nothing on top today, so under Stripe Connect 'separate charges and transfers' Stripe's 2.9% + 30c comes out of platformCents. On a $55.56 backing (the $50 payout minimum) that turns the $3.18 we keep into about $1.27; on a $10 monthly backing it leaves about 41c before Connect fees. Change: add a processing line item at backing checkout (and offer bank debit, 0.8% capped $5, for larger gifts), make sure grossCents passed to splitBacking excludes the processing line, and run it in Stripe test mode. Touches convex/garden/stripe.ts checkout creation and stripeHandlers.ts recordBackingPayment. Related: PR #15, docs/features/backing-payouts.md (PR #17), bead wonderwall-7avu.

title: Payout rail: owed/paid ledger for backings + Stripe Connect Express for creatives and hosts
description: Money OUT has no rail. Money IN is live on every lane (membership, coverage codes, pledges, products, pool contributions). What exists for money out: hostPayouts + recordHostPayout (app/convex/garden/products.ts) — a MANUAL owed-vs-paid ledger for community-product sales only, with an operator form. Project backings (projectSupport, projects.raisedCents) have NO owed/paid row at all: the creative's 90% sits on the platform's Stripe balance untracked. Zero Stripe Connect code anywhere. Specified in docs/phase-1b/spec.md §5 (manual transfers for October, Connect Express in Phase 3), the-garden-product-plan.md §2.4 (no paid-table pricing before the payout path exists) and §3 (a project_contribution ledger type that was never added to grantContributions.type). title: Gated event video link + join proxy + calendar invite (free/public)
description:
SPEC: docs/gated-event-video-prd.md. Ships free/public event video now: organizer pastes their own stream link (YouTube Live or any), attendees join via a stable /j/{eventId} proxy, recording link posted after. Paid gating deliberately NOT in this pass — when the first genuinely paid event appears, pull LiveKit forward (wonderwall-99kd) instead of shipping honor-system gating on a forwardable link.

Three verified code facts this build depends on: (1) convex/events.ts spreads the raw event doc in three queries (list:53, get:120, search:466), two of them unauthenticated public browse — so meetingUrl/recordingUrl live in a SEPARATE eventVideo table, never on events; (2) rsvpToEvent (convex/garden/eventRsvps.ts:96) is unauthenticated, so an RSVP row is never a credential; (3) nothing in the codebase ever writes events.status 'completed', so recording posting is organizer-driven with no completion trigger.

The /j/{eventId} proxy is the strategically important piece: calendar invites carry the proxy URL, not the real one, so invites already sitting in attendees' calendars survive the later switch to LiveKit token minting. Built as a CF Pages Function following the working precedent at app/functions/events/[id].ts. Calendar invites are net-new — no ics/VCALENDAR code exists anywhere today.

title: Events video hosting (LiveKit): public + paid access tiers — due 2026-09-06
description:
SPEC: docs/events-video-hosting-prd.md (revised 2026-08-30 after codebase verification). Build from that file, not from this description. Deadline 2026-09-06.

Supersedes this bead's prior "defer until a call is scheduled" posture. The trigger arrived: Rick wants public AND paid event video hosting inside one week, and LiveKit Cloud is now a provisioned, paid $50/mo Ship-tier account — a sunk cost, not a future decision. Provider question is closed: LiveKit for in-app interactive video across Events, Offerings, and (later) Table sessions.

What this bead is now: Events video hosting, week one. Add a video room to an event, with two access tiers — "public" (anyone with the link) and "paid" (organizer-confirmed RSVP only, off-platform payment link, no charge verification, matching offerings.externalPaymentLinkUrl / projectSupport.status). No Stripe: convex/garden/stripe.ts exists but is the Host-org coverage lane only; per-event ticketing stays blocked on wonderwall-sxi.

What this bead's ORIGINAL reasoning still holds, and the spec preserves: the 200x WebRTC cost trap for large passive audiences is a delivery-shape argument, not a vendor argument, and it is still true on LiveKit. The spec makes this a decision rather than an open question: cut LiveKit egress, ship the WebRTC room with maxParticipants: 50, and if the first public event needs to be bigger than that, use a YouTube Live link on the event page — exactly this bead's original recommendation, zero build. Building an egress pipeline under a one-week deadline would be worse on cost (your own S3/CDN bill, not the $50), time, and risk.

Cost correction worth carrying: the "$50/mo covers Year-1 including HLS" reading of video-provider-research.md is oversold. That research's Year-1 scenario consumed 116,910 of the 150,000 included participant-minutes on Table sessions alone (~33k/month headroom = about eleven 50-person hours), assumed a capacity-planned usage shape rather than an open-ended public Events feature, and excludes your-own-bucket egress bandwidth. Hence the mandatory maxParticipants cap.

Week-one scope (see spec for detail):
1. Day-1 spike: LIVEKIT_API_KEY/LIVEKIT_API_SECRET into Convex env (neither exists today), prove a token mints and a browser joins. Decide livekit-server-sdk vs. hand-rolled HS256 JWT here — the SDK's Convex-runtime compatibility is the highest-variance unknown, and a LiveKit token is just an HS256 JWT signable with WebCrypto in ~25 lines, avoiding a "use node" split (convex/garden/stripe.ts:4 documents that a "use node" file is actions-only).
2. Schema: events gets videoEnabled/accessType/priceCents/paymentLinkUrl/roomName; eventRsvps gets paymentStatus/paymentConfirmedAt/paymentConfirmedBy (verified: events at schema.ts:131-168 has no price/access field, eventRsvps at schema.ts:907 has no status field at all).
3. resolveVideoAccess returning a role ("host" | "participant" | "blocked"), unioning eventRsvps AND accepted eventApplications — approval-required events route attendance through applications, and an eventRsvps-only rule would deny every accepted applicant. Mirrors announcements.ts resolveAudience's switch idiom.
4. Organizer composer UI for the access-tier fields.
5. confirmRsvpPayment mutation + organizer roster UI. SHIPPING BLOCKER: without it paymentStatus never reaches "confirmed" and nobody can ever join a paid event. Organizer-only (event.organizerId check). Note rsvpToEvent lives at convex/garden/eventRsvps.ts:96, not convex/events.ts, and is UNAUTHENTICATED — anyone can create an RSVP row with any email, so RSVP existence is never a credential.
6. <VideoRoomPanel> on app/routes/event.tsx + a pre-check query so the page shows Join / Pay to join / nothing without minting a token.

Token security (a leaked room token is a live A/V feed and a billing surface, unlike the text-only honor-system cases): mint per-request, never per-event; identity must be unique and stable (user:{userId}, rsvp:{rsvpId} for guests — eventRsvps.userId is optional) because LiveKit enforces one live connection per identity per room, which does most of the anti-sharing work; 10-minute TTL (default is ~6h; TTL gates joining only, so it costs joined users nothing); maxParticipants cap; explicit grants, never roomCreate or roomAdmin on attendee tokens.

Correction that would otherwise ship broken: canPublish: false genuinely prevents publishing — there is no room config that overrides a token grant. Attendees need canPublish: true; the host needs roomAdmin: true for mute/remove (canPublish: true alone does not grant moderation).

Announcements interaction: adding optional eventRsvps.paymentStatus does not break resolveAudience (convex/announcements.ts:169). One deliberate semantic change — a paid event's broadcasts will reach "pending" RSVPs too, which is the natural channel for sending the payment link. Do not add a payment filter to resolveAudience.

Out of scope: HLS/egress, recording/VOD, refunds, per-event Stripe, Table-session migration.
notes: SUPERSEDED FOR WEEK ONE by docs/gated-event-video-prd.md (2026-08-31). Decision: ship free/public events on an organizer-pasted link (YouTube Live or any) now, with a /j/{eventId} join proxy; pull LiveKit forward when the first genuinely PAID event appears, rather than shipping honor-system gating on a forwardable link. This bead remains the LiveKit build and its trigger is now the first paid event, not the 2026-09-06 date. Key carry-forward: the join proxy is a CF Pages Function that makes the LiveKit switch non-breaking — calendar invites already in attendees' calendars keep working because only the server-side redirect target changes.

title: Queue Processor - Crawl Engine
description:
Build the core engine that processes the crawler queue.

## Functionality
1. Read pending URLs from crawlerQueue
2. Respect rate limits per source (requestsPerMinute from crawlerSources)
3. Call classifyUrl action for each URL
4. Update queue item status (completed/failed)
5. Handle retries with exponential backoff
6. Record crawler run stats

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Convex Scheduled Function
- Use ctx.scheduler to process queue items
- Self-rescheduling loop
- Pros: Simple, no external infra
- Cons: Limited concurrency, cold starts

### Option B: Convex Action with External Trigger
- HTTP endpoint that processes N items
- Called by external cron (Cloudflare Worker, Vercel Cron)
- Pros: More control, can run longer
- Cons: Need external scheduler

### Recommended: Option A for MVP
- Create `processQueue` internal action
- Processes 1-5 URLs per invocation
- Schedules itself for next batch after delay
- Respects source-specific rate limits

## Error Handling
- Max 3 retries per URL
- Exponential backoff: 1min, 5min, 30min
- After max retries, mark as failed with error message
- Alert (console log) on repeated failures

## Convex Functions Needed
- `internal.crawler.processNextBatch` - main processor
- `internal.crawler.scheduleNextRun` - self-scheduling
- `crawler.startQueueProcessor` - manual trigger from admin
- `crawler.stopQueueProcessor` - pause processing
- `crawler.getQueueStatus` - query for admin UI
close_reason: Queue processor complete with batch processing, retry logic, and admin UI. Upgraded to Llama 3.3 70B with json_schema structured output.

## SMS Auth UX Research (2026 Best Practices)

1. Validate invite code first

- Use react-phone-number-input library (handles country codes, E.164 format)
- Auto-detect user's country
- Store in E.164 format (+12133734253)
- inputmode='numeric' and autocomplete='tel' attributes

- 6 digits (industry standard)
- 2-5 minute expiry
- Auto-advance between digit fields
- Support paste and SMS autofill (autocomplete='one-time-code')
- Auto-submit when complete
- Show countdown timer and resend option

### Security (Critical):
- Rate limit: 1 SMS per 30 sec, max 3 per 15 min per phone
- Max 3-5 code attempts before lockout
- Use crypto.randomInt() for code generation

- POST /transactionalSMS/sms endpoint
- Include sender name, recipient (E.164), content with code
- Handle delivery status callbacks

title: Add session video to Offerings (LiveKit, shares the Events room module) — week two
description:
SPEC: docs/events-video-hosting-prd.md (revised 2026-08-30). Week TWO — deliberately cut from the 2026-09-06 one-week scope. Depends on wonderwall-99kd (Events video) landing first.

PROVIDER DECISION SUPERSEDED. This bead previously specified Daily.co and an offerings.meetingUrl link field, mirroring the D8 Table-session decision. That is void. LiveKit Cloud is now a provisioned, paid $50/mo account, and the product runs one video stack: Offerings uses the same LiveKit room, the same token minter, and the same <VideoRoomPanel> as Events. Do not add a second provider, and do not add offerings.meetingUrl — add offerings.roomName + offerings.videoEnabled, matching the events fields. (Related stale reference: gardenTables.meetingUrl's schema comment still reads "(D8: Daily.co)" — fix that line whenever Tables are next touched.)

Why this is week two rather than week one: it is the largest single saving (~2 days) in a schedule that does not otherwise fit, and it carries a blocker that Events does not.

BLOCKER — offeringSignups.status CANNOT be used for payment gating. The original bead's scope item 3 proposed gating on an offeringSignups row, and the first draft of the PRD proposed reusing "pledged"/"confirmed" directly. Both are wrong. From convex/offerings.ts:318:

    const status = isFree || offering.externalPaymentLinkUrl ? "confirmed" : "pledged";

Status is decided at insert time, before any money moves, and nothing in the codebase ever patches it afterward (verified — no mutation writes offeringSignups.status after creation). Consequences:
- Paid offering WITH an external payment link: every signup is instantly "confirmed". Gating on "confirmed" is equivalent to no gating at all, for exactly the paid case this exists to serve.
- Paid offering WITHOUT a link: every signup is "pledged" forever, with no path to "confirmed". Gating on "confirmed" locks those people out permanently, with no organizer UI to fix it.

offeringSignups.status answers "how did this signup originate," not "did this person pay." (announcements.ts gets this right — it treats pledged and confirmed identically.) So Offerings needs its own organizer-confirmed payment field AND its own organizer confirm UI — a second copy of the confirmRsvpPayment work in wonderwall-99kd, on a surface with a different ownership check (offering.userId, plus an isAdmin bypass that events does not have) and a required rather than optional userId.

Reuse, honestly scoped: share the token minter and the <VideoRoomPanel> component. Do NOT try to share the eligibility resolver's per-surface lookups — Events and Offerings differ on ownership field, guest support, admin bypass, and the meaning of "confirmed." One resolveVideoAccess function with a switch (mirroring announcements.ts resolveAudience) is the right amount of sharing. Let the Events implementation land first and tell you where the seam actually is; building the abstraction across two surfaces when only one exists is how the deadline gets lost.

Still true from the original bead: offerings has remote/cadence/externalPaymentLinkUrl but zero video field, and app/routes/offerings.tsx has no join-a-session UI, so a Patron who signs up for a remote class has no in-app way to attend. Zoom remains a bad fit for the same per-host-seat reason ("any Creative running an Offering" means many individual hosts).

title: Career Page Job Scraper
description:
Scrape actual job listings from organization career pages.

## Context
The crawler identifies organizations with career pages (has_careers_page=true). This feature extracts the actual job postings from those pages.

## Functionality
1. For orgs with has_careers_page=true, find their careers URL
2. Fetch and parse the careers page
3. Extract job listings: title, department, location, description, apply URL
4. Store jobs linked to the crawledOrganization
5. Mark jobs as "crawled" vs "posted" (by org directly)

## Career Page Patterns
- `/careers`, `/jobs`, `/careers/openings`
- Greenhouse, Lever, Workday, BambooHR embeds
- Custom career pages with job listings

## Job Schema Fields
- title, department, location (city/state/remote)
- employmentType (full-time, part-time, contract)
- salaryRange (if disclosed)
- description (truncated)
- applyUrl
- postedDate, expiresDate
- sourceType: "crawled" | "posted"
- crawledOrganizationId (link to org)

## Technical Approach
- After org classification, if has_careers_page, schedule job scrape
- Use common patterns to find job listings
- Store raw HTML for debugging
- Handle JS-rendered pages (Greenhouse, Lever APIs if possible)

## Edge Cases
- ATS systems with APIs (Greenhouse, Lever) - use API if available
- Paginated job listings
- Jobs with no posted date
- Duplicate detection (same job, new crawl)
close_reason: Job scraper implemented with career page detection, ATS pattern matching, AI extraction, and leadership markdown storage.

title: Source Parsers - Directory Scrapers
description:
Build parsers to extract organization URLs from configured directories.

## Sources to Support

### 1. PublicSquare Marketplace
- URL: publicsquare.com/marketplace
- Structure: Category pages with business listings
- Extract: Business name, website, category
- Pagination: Load more / infinite scroll
- Rate limit: 10 req/min

### 2. Church Finder Directory
- URL: churchchurch.com or similar
- Structure: State > City > Church listings
- Extract: Church name, website, address, denomination
- Pagination: Standard page links
- Rate limit: 5 req/min

### 3. Christian Jobs Board
- URL: christianjobs.com or similar
- Structure: Job listings with employer info
- Extract: Employer name, website, industry
- Pagination: Standard
- Rate limit: 10 req/min

### 4. Kingdom Advisors Network
- URL: kingdomadvisors.com
- Structure: Member directory
- Extract: Advisor name, firm, website
- Monthly crawl only
- Rate limit: 5 req/min

## Implementation Approach
- Each source gets a parser function
- Parser returns array of {url, metadata}
- Metadata includes: name (if found), source, category
- URLs added to queue via bulkAddToQueue

## Technical
- Use fetch with proper headers
- Handle JS-rendered pages (may need Puppeteer for some)
- Respect robots.txt
- Store raw HTML for debugging

## Convex Functions
- `crawler.crawlSource` action - takes sourceId, runs parser
- `internal.crawler.parsePublicSquare`

title: Crawler Scheduler - Automated Runs
description:
Automate crawler runs based on source configuration.

## Scheduling Logic
Each source has:
- crawlFrequency: "daily", "weekly", "monthly", "manual"
- lastCrawledAt: timestamp
- isActive: boolean

Scheduler checks which sources are due and triggers crawls.

## Implementation Options

### Option A: Convex Crons (Recommended)
- Use Convex cron jobs feature
- Single cron runs every hour
- Checks which sources need crawling
- Queues URLs for due sources

### Option B: External Scheduler
- Cloudflare Worker with cron trigger
- Calls Convex HTTP endpoint
- More flexibility but external dependency

## Scheduler Logic
```
every hour:
  for each active source:
    if shouldCrawl(source):
      await crawlSource(source.id)
      updateLastCrawledAt(source.id)

shouldCrawl(source):
  if source.crawlFrequency === "manual": return false
  timeSinceLastCrawl = now - source.lastCrawledAt
  return timeSinceLastCrawl > frequencyToMs(source.crawlFrequency)
```

## Convex Functions
- `crons.ts` - define hourly cron
- `internal.crawler.checkScheduledCrawls` - main scheduler logic
- Update `crawlerSources` mutation to set lastCrawledAt

## Admin UI
- Show next scheduled crawl per source
- Override: "Skip next" or "Run now"
- Enable/disable scheduler globally

title: Design: Social connection metaphor (connect vs follow vs friend)
description:
Explore what social connection metaphor best fits Wonderwall's community of Christian creatives.

## Current State
- App has "Favorites" (one-way, bookmark-style)
- No mutual connection system yet
- Invite-only community with network stats

## Options to Consider

### 1. "Connect" (LinkedIn-style)
**Pros:**
- Implies mutual, bi-directional relationship
- Professional tone fits creative professionals
- Suggests collaboration potential
- More intimate than "follow"

**Cons:**
- Requires acceptance (adds friction)
- Can feel transactional/corporate
- Doesn't scale for creators with many admirers
- "Connection request pending" feels formal

### 2. "Follow" (Twitter/Instagram-style)
**Pros:**
- Familiar UX, low friction
- One-directional, no acceptance needed
- Scales well for popular creators
- Clear, understood paradigm

**Cons:**
- Impersonal, platform-y
- Implies hierarchy (follower vs followed)
- "Follower" has negative connotations for some Christians
- Doesn't encourage reciprocity

### 3. "Friend" (Facebook-style)
**Pros:**
- Warm, personal tone
- Fits community-focused values
- Implies mutual care

**Cons:**
- Requires acceptance (friction)
- "Unfriend" feels harsh
- Can feel dated/juvenile
- Awkward mixing personal + professional

### 4. Creative Alternatives

**"Crew" / "Add to Crew"**
- Fits production/creative industry language
- Implies collaboration, working together
- Could be asymmetric ("They're on my crew")

**"Circle" / "Inner Circle"**
- Community-oriented language
- Tiered possibilities (close circle vs wider)
- Google+ baggage though

**"Know" / "I know them"**
- Authentic real-world language
- "People you know" feels natural
- Awkward as action verb

**"Admire"**
- Positive, non-hierarchical
- Fits appreciating others' work
- One-way, like favorites

### 5. Keep Enhanced Favorites
- Don't add new system
- "Favorites" already works
- Add mutual indicator ("You're both favorites")
- Simplest approach

## Recommendation Considerations
- Community is invite-only, already somewhat intimate
- Christian values: mutual respect, not hierarchy
- Creative professionals: collaboration > fandom
- App name "Wonderwall" could inspire themed language

## Questions to Resolve
1. Do we need mutual connections, or is one-way sufficient?
2. Should connections unlock features (DMs, etc)?
3. How does this interact with existing Favorites?
4. What's the notification/acceptance UX?
